definition: Running several attention operations in parallel with separate projections, letting the model attend to different relationship types simultaneously (syntax in one head, coreference in another), then concatenating the results.
details: Running several attention operations in parallel with separate projections, letting the model attend to different relationship types simultaneously (syntax in one head, coreference in another), then concatenating the results.

explainer.lead: Multi-head attention runs several attention operations in parallel with separate projections, then concatenates the results. It matters because it lets a model attend to different relationship types at once, such as syntax in one head and coreference in another.

tiers.eli5: Think of several readers going through the same sentence at once, each watching for a different kind of connection, then pooling what they noticed. One tracks grammar, another tracks who 'she' refers to.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on parallel heads with separate projections to capture multiple relationship types simultaneously, then concatenate the outputs. The value lies in attending to different relationship types at once rather than a single view.
tiers.paperLevel: Several attention operations run in parallel with separate projections, each attending to different relationship types simultaneously, and the results are concatenated.

explainer.example: In one sentence, one head tracks syntax while another tracks coreference, and their outputs are concatenated into a single representation.
